sources.citation: Lescarbot, Marc. 1609. Histoire de la Nouvelle France. Paris: Jean Milot. Book VI, ch. 6, numeral table 'Les Souriquois disent / Les Etechemins' (John Carter Brown Library copy, scanned text).
sources.note: Primary and only attestation of the language: a bare list of the numerals 1-10 (Bechkon, Nich, Nach, Iau, Prenchk, Chachit, Coutachit, Erouiguen, Pechcoquem, Peiock). No diacritics, no remark on accent or pronunciation.
Classification 'Unclassifiable', extinct, ISO etc; no descriptive references listed at all (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).
Individual language, extinct; no references beyond Ethnologue/Glottolog/Wikipedia.

States the only known record is Lescarbot's numerals 1-10; as a set they match no other Algonquian language; all other records called 'Etchemin' are Maliseet-Passamaquoddy. Cites Asher & Moseley (eds.) 2007 Atlas of the World's Languages p. 14 and the Lescarbot editions. Nothing on stress.

sources.note: Draws on Lescarbot's Micmac vocabulary for Basque loans; does not mention Etchemin at all; nothing on stress.
